According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, Apple is making major changes to its retail stores in preparation for the upcoming Home lineup. At the very least, Apple should be launching a brand-new HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K this fall, but the changes suggest a third, even more important product may be in the pipeline.

Apple has been sitting on a large backlog of Home products, primarily because the Siri revamp has been delayed time and again. Now that Siri is finally ready, these products, which haven't been updated in years, are expected to finally see the light of day.

That said, earlier reports indicated that Apple would launch the new HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K first, while its first smart home hub (also known as the HomePod with display or HomePad) might arrive later.

However, based on the current preparations at retail stores, this smart home hub could launch alongside the updated Apple TV and HomePod mini. Excerpt from the Power On newsletter:

Of course, the exact answer will only come on the day Apple holds its September event. However, based on today's report, it looks like we'll soon get a glimpse of Apple's brand-new smart home hub, alongside a new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini with support for Siri AI.

Summary

Based on current rumours, Apple's smart home hub will feature a 7-inch square display and come in two versions: one with built-in speakers, and another with magnets on the back for wall mounting. The product will run an entirely new operating system with a home screen that supports widgets, and in addition to serving as a FaceTime device, it will act as the hub for all the user's smart home accessories and Siri. It is also said to be powered by the A18 chip.

Another new rumour in the Home lineup is that the new Apple TV 4K may come with an all-new Siri Remote, though the specific changes remain unclear.

Are you interested in the new Home lineup? Which one are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
